'''Sample matrix inversion''' (or '''direct matrix inversion''') is an [[algorithm]] that estimates weights of an array ([[adaptive filter]]) by replacing the [[correlation matrix]] <math>R</math> with its estimate. Using <math>K</math> <math>N</math>-dimensional samples <math>X_1, X_2,\dots,X_K</math>, an unbiased estimate of <math>R_{X}</math>, the <math>N \times N</math> correlation matrix of the array signals, may be obtained by means of a simple [[averaging]] scheme:
:<math>\hat{R}_{X} = \frac{1}{K} \sum\limits_{k=1}^K X_k X^H_k,</math>
where <math>H</math> is the [[conjugate transpose]]. The expression of the theoretically optimal weights requires the [[inverse matrix|inverse]] of <math>R_{X}</math>, and the inverse of the estimates matrix is then used for finding estimated optimal weights.
